newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MAN TO ANSWER CHARGES IN RELATION TO EXTORTION ATTEMPT
A 33-year-old Melbourne man has been charged in relation to an alleged extortion attempt against food company Nestle.
Mark James Milton, of Orchard Crescent, Box Hill, appeared before a bail justice at the Melbourne Custody Centre early this morning.
He's been charged by New South Wales detectives on a provisional warrant of demanding money with menaces and was remanded in custody to appear at Melbourne Magistrate's Court later today.
New South Wales detectives will apply for his extradition at this morning's court hearing.
The arrest follows a 13 day operation after Nestle in Sydney was allegedly told its products would be contaminated unless a large sum of money was paid.
UNIVERSITY OF NSW "PEACEFUL" PROTEST LEADS TO ARRESTS
The National Union of Students says eight students were arrested last night while protesting aganist a decision by the University of New South Wales to introduce up-front fees.
The University Council voted last night to support the introduction of fees from next year.
NUS President, Andrew Bourke, says eight students were arrested when they tried to "peacefully prevent" councillors who supported fees from leaving the university building.
Mr Bourke says the decision will drive a wedge through student morale.
University Vice-Chancellor, John Niland, says the vote was one for the university's survival and not a vote for fees.
Professor Niland says in an environment of declining funding from the Federal Government, tough decisions like this have to be made.
He says the university has only approved a limited number of fee paying students for next year.
TELSTRA WORKER "THREATENED WITH SACK" AFTER PM INTERVIEW
The Community and Public Sector Union says a Telstra worker who expressed fears about an impending cut to maritime distress signal monitoring services has been threatened with the sack.
Dirk Veldhoen spoke to ABC Radio's PM programme on Friday.
The union says he received a letter from Telstra within two hours, asking him to explain his conduct.
The union's Adrian O'Connell says the company wants a response within 48 hours, but Mr O'Connell says this is ludicrous, because Telstra hasn't been specific about the alleged misconduct.
He says the company needs to tell Mr Veldhoen, a Perth union delegate, what it found offensive about his conduct before he can reply.
ECOLOGIST SLAMS BHP'S "GREED"
An internationally renowned ecologist has labelled BHP a corporate hijacker.
Vandana Shiva addressed delegates yesterday during the five-day Pathways to Sustainability conference in Newcastle.
Dr Shiva says people are being made to believe migrants escalate unemployment rather than the greed of corporations.
She says BHP, like other global companies, fails to recognise its wealth was built on the local environment and labour of its workers.
300 INVOLVED IN RIOT AT SUPER LEAGUE MATCH
In Sydney, more than 70 police were called-in to break up a riot at a Super League match at Belmore last night, after a controversial decision was made by the referee.
Police say the brawl broke out after a Canterbury try was disallowed in the second half of the match against Penrith.
They say spectators began throwing bottles and cans at each other and on to the field, and then at police when they tried to restore order.
One police officer and about a dozen spectators received minor injuries.
MILES FRANKLIN COULD GO TO FORMER WINNER
Two previous winners of the prestigious Miles Franklin literary award are among finalists for this year's prize to be announced in Sydney tonight.
Making the shortlist for the second time are Thea Astley for her novel "The Multiple Effects of Rainshadow", and David Malouf for "The Conversations at Curlow Creek".

Other finalists are Robert Dessaix for "Night Letters", Robert Drewe for "The Drowner", David Foster for "The Glade Within The Grove", Janette Turner Hospital for "Oyster", and John Scott for "Before I Wake".
